title: Gilbert N. Lewis, Fritz Haber & R.B. Woodward (1875–1946 / 1868–1934 / 1917–1979) — Haber-Bosch, Ypres, the Covalent Bond, 41 Nobel Snubs, Vitamin B₁₂, and Orbital Symmetry

teenKit.tldr: Chemistry gave us the power to feed the world from thin air and map molecular bonds, but also birthed horrific wartime weapons and broke the brilliant minds who unlocked them.
teenKit.whyItMatters: The food on your plate, the medicine in your cabinet, and the electronic screens you stare at all exist because these brilliant, deeply flawed scientists figured out how atoms share and rearrange themselves.
keyTakeaways: Fritz Haber literally conjured fertilizer out of thin air to feed billions of people, yet later weaponized chemistry by designing lethal chlorine gas for World War I.
Gilbert N. Lewis drew the electron-dot structures you still use in school, yet suffered the ultimate academic heartbreak of being nominated for the Nobel Prize 41 times and never winning.
R.B. Woodward treated complex organic synthesis like fine art, building life-saving molecules and natural wonders atom by atom.

vocab.meaning: An industrial method that pulls nitrogen gas straight from the atmosphere and turns it into ammonia to make mass-production crop fertilizer.
A chemical link where two atoms share a pair of electrons to stay tightly locked together.
A fast-acting, highly lethal poison gas that suffocates human cells from the inside out by blocking oxygen use.
The mathematical rulebook created by R.B. Woodward and Roald Hoffmann that predicts how organic molecules will twist and bond during reactions.

quiz.question: What tragic distinction belongs to Gilbert N. Lewis regarding the Nobel Prize?
options: He refused it every time he was offered.
He was nominated 41 times but never won a single one.
He won it twice for work he actually stole from students.
He was stripped of his prize after his death.
quiz.explanation: Lewis was nominated an incredible 41 times by his scientific peers, yet politics and rivalries kept him from ever taking home the medal.

quiz.question: What dual legacy defines Fritz Haber's impact on human history?
options: He invented the plastic water bottle and discovered penicillin.
He mapped out DNA and created the first atomic bomb.
He invented a process to feed the global population, but also pioneered weaponized poison gas.
He discovered the electron and invented chemical warfare protection gear.
quiz.explanation: Haber's nitrogen fixation process literally feeds billions of people today, but he also personally oversaw the terrifying use of chlorine gas at Ypres.

quiz.question: What chemical emergency unfolded in Gilbert N. Lewis's Berkeley laboratory in 1946?
options: A radioactive uranium leak melted through the floor.
An explosion of nitroglycerin leveled the entire chemistry building.
A shattered glass vacuum line leaked deadly hydrogen cyanide gas, leading to his death.
A massive fire destroyed decades of his unpublished journals.
quiz.explanation: Lewis was found dead in his lab beside a broken glass vacuum line leaking hydrogen cyanide, bringing a dark end to a brilliant career.
